findings.description: The `b -> .` case in the new `it.each` never goes through `b`. The link sits at `src/x.ts`, so `b/b/...` resolves from `checkout/src`, where there is no `b`. The old lexical check also lands outside, so this case passes without the fix and only the node_modules case tells the two apart. A target like `'../b/b/../escape'` does go through the root `b`: the old code kept it, the new code refuses it. The `startsWith('b/')` guard would need changing to match.

The `it.each` hides a per-case setup difference behind `if (target.startsWith('b/')) commitLink(worktree, 'b', '.')`, so the test body branches on the data string. A third case column, such as a `links` array, would state the setup directly.

The comment above the new `it.each` repeats the implementation comment in `refuseEscapingLinks`, naming the same two cases, which the case labels and title already carry. Delete it or reduce it to a pointer.

Decision 81 says a dangling link is "judged by where it points". It doesn't mention that a dangling target with a `..` after a named segment is now refused outright. The sentence is still true, just incomplete.

The conventions reviewer says it did not open general.md, naming.md or docs/09-decisions.md, so the delta was checked only against testing.md and the AGENTS.md comment rules, not against decision 81.
